label: UniFi 8 PoE (Gen1)
description: UniFi 8 PoE (Gen1) (US-8-60W) - 8x 1G RJ45 (4 PoE). 48 W PoE budget; 16 Gbps switching capacity.

poe.note: 48 W, the vendor's own aggregate row: "Max. PoE Output = Up to PoE / Total PoE Availability = 48W" beside "Port Layout = 1 GbE RJ45 8 (4 PoE) (1G/100M/10M)" and "PoE Ports = 4 / Max. PoE Wattage per Port by PSE = PoE 15.4W" (read 2026-11-19). The model name says 60W, and the engine had been parsing 60 W out of "US-8-60W" -- 12 W of PoE this adapter cannot supply, against the 48 W the description and this note both state. Same page: Switching Capacity 16 Gbps, Total Non-Blocking Throughput 8 Gbps, Max. Power Consumption 12W excluding PoE output. The vendor prints "8 (4 PoE)", so the four data-only ports say poeOut: 0: this label contains "PoE", and engine/media.js isPoePse() powers every copper port of a switch that claims PSE, which made all eight of them 15.4 W PSEs - 123.2 W of declared PSE capacity on a 48 W budget.
